title: Further squeeze: even an infallible Pope or Council cannot prove its own legitimacy or pure decrees
source_text: XXXVII. Deinde sic urgebo, ut fides mea certum fundamentum habeat, non tantum necesse est ut sciam Ecclesiam infallibile testimonium perhibere, sive per Concilium, sive per summum Pontificem; sed praeterea ut certus sim legitimum esse Pontificem illum cujus testimonium audio, & legitimum quoque Concilium cujus decreta mihi objiciuntur. De hoc autem non possum certus reddi per testimonium sive Pontificis, sive Concilii ipsius. Nam proprio testimonio sufficienter nihil probari potest. Ac praeterea posito quod talis Pontifex fuerit legitimus, & legitimum tale Concilium, oportet ut certus sim sincerum & incorruptum ad manus meas pervenisse Pontificis decretum, & similiter sinceros & incorruptos Canones Concilii. Itaque necesse est ut non tantum praeter Scripturam & traditiones, sed etiam praeter ipsa Pontificum decreta, & Conciliorum Canones, sit in Ecclesia quoddam Dei verbum, quo certus reddar legitimum esse Pontificem istum, & Concilium istud, & decreta Pontificum, ac Conciliorum statuta, quae mihi in manus traduntur, sincera esse atque incorrupta, alioqui fides mea non nitetur certo fundamento, neque fides dicenda erit, quandoquidem fides verbo Dei nititur.
pass_a_gloss: Then I will press thus, that my faith may have a certain foundation, it is necessary not only that I know that the Church bears infallible testimony, whether through a Council or through the supreme Pontiff; but moreover that I be certain that that Pontiff is legitimate whose testimony I hear, and also that that Council is legitimate whose decrees are objected to me. But concerning this I cannot be made certain by the testimony either of the Pontiff or of the Council itself. For by its own testimony nothing can be sufficiently proved. And moreover, granted that such a Pontiff was legitimate, and such a Council legitimate, it is necessary that I be certain that the Pontiff's decree has come to my hands sincere and uncorrupted, and likewise the Canons of the Council sincere and uncorrupted. Therefore it is necessary that not only besides Scripture and traditions, but also besides the very decrees of Pontiffs and Canons of Councils, there be in the Church some word of God by which I may be made certain that that Pontiff is legitimate, and that Council, and that the decrees of Pontiffs and statutes of Councils which are delivered into my hands are sincere and uncorrupted, otherwise my faith will not rest on a certain foundation, nor will it be to be called faith, since faith rests on the word of God.
pass_b_english: For faith to rest sure, you need more than an infallible Pope or Council — you need certainty that this Pope and this Council are the legitimate ones.
Neither can prove its own legitimacy by its own testimony.
Even if legitimacy is granted, you still need certainty that the decrees and canons reached you uncorrupted.
So Rome's rule would demand yet another divine word beyond Scripture, tradition, papal decrees, and conciliar canons — or faith has no sure foundation.

lemmas.latin: proprio testimonio sufficienter nihil probari potest
lemmas.gloss: by its own testimony nothing can be sufficiently proved

choices.english: faith rests on the word of God
choices.why: Without a divine ground it is not faith.
rejected: faith can rest on bare institutional claim
